# Automatic standalone four-deck bridge

This beta pairs the XDJ-XZ 1.26 runtime with a RAM-only USB helper and GPL-2.0-only hub module. The source supports either arrangement: music in top USB1 with the rear USB-B loopback cable in top USB2, or music in USB2 with the cable in USB1. These arrangements have offline host/ARM coverage; the new USB1-music arrangement still needs physical-controller acceptance.

The helper requires one music mount and verifies its physical top-port ancestry. Two mounted music drives are ambiguous and prevent admission. It pins the opposite top port as the loopback target for that process lifetime. Native decks must be stopped before module admission and USB binding. Changing or removing the admitted music drive permanently retires that helper's binding; the helper never switches ports during playback.

The module requires the read-only parameter `loopback_port=1` or `loopback_port=2`. Missing or invalid selection fails before notifier registration. It accepts only the exact XZ loopback hub/topology on that port. It can adopt an already enumerated hub only while unbound and childless, with a retained CONFIGURED or SUSPENDED configuration. The music port is never locked or modified by the module's existing-hub scan. Physical disconnection restores the owned metadata and releases its references; a configured driver unbind alone does not count as physical disconnection. There is no forced unload.

The helper retains the existing boot, application/runtime, kernel ABI, mount, descriptor and volume-identity checks. FAT16/FAT32, exFAT and HFS+/HFSX rules and later-partition handling are unchanged. Serial absence is recorded explicitly; it is never replaced with an invented identity. Legacy diagnostic IDs containing `USB2` remain stable for status/report readers, but their validation follows the selected music port.

Execution remains under the USB loader. The existing bootstrap stages the helper, module and runtime under `/dev/shm`; the helper verifies RAM paths and the exact paired runtime before admission. The module changes only volatile hub metadata and restores it on physical disconnection. No firmware installation, persistent boot change, or music-drive write is introduced. The music drive must remain connected while the route runs.

The Windows package includes licenses/xz-hub-source.tar.gz with the complete retained kernel source, configuration, local compiler compatibility header, module and build recipes. The same archive accompanies the beta release. Extract it into a fresh directory and run bash build-module.sh using ARM GNU EABI GCC13, GNU binutils, make and Python3. CRCs are derived from recompiling source; live CRC substitution is not used. The kernel build directory is disposable.

build_bridge.py accepts --payload, --module, --sha-source, --zig and --output. Supply your locally prepared supported application/runtime payload, the built module directory and mods/audio/vendor/sha256. It derives exact hashes/ABI pins and compiles a staged source copy against that generated contract, then checks the ARM32 GLIBC2.4 build with QEMU. Rebuilding a helper/module requires refreshing the USB-loader resource and bootstrap hashes together; existing packaged bytes remain pinned. Proprietary firmware, application binaries and boot keys are not included in corresponding source.

`verify_binding.py --output SCRATCH [--arm]` runs the helper against in-memory filesystem/process fixtures with live operations forbidden. `bash verify-module.sh SCRATCH` runs both port orientations under host ASan/UBSan, ARM/QEMU and host TSan, including ownership, invalid selection, notifier races and physical-disconnect cleanup. Each command requires a new scratch directory outside the source tree.

detach.S is GPL-2.0-only and builds with arm-linux-gnueabi-gcc -nostdlib -static -no-pie -march=armv7-a -marm -Wl,--build-id=none detach.S -o detach. The bridge is MIT-licensed; its SHA256 implementation retains its own public-domain notice under mods/audio/vendor/sha256.

Offline lifecycle and sanitizer tests plus exact on-device read-only qualification do not establish audible playback, kernel scheduling under every workload or complete four-deck performance acceptance. The beta release notes list remaining limitations.
